findings.claim: Space is now preventDefault-ed (keydown and keyup) on window for the whole page lifetime, including the start, pause and results screens. Those screens focus a native button and rely on Space/Enter to activate it, so Space no longer activates RACE, RESUME or NEXT RACE on any track.
findings.evidence: keyboard.ts:52-57 `if (k.code === ACTION_KEY) { k.preventDefault(); down.add(k.code); actionTapped = true; return; }` and :64 `if (down.delete(k.code)) k.preventDefault();`. game.ts:115 creates the Input once, on the default window target, with no mode/paused gating. dom.ts:75 `overlay.show()` focuses the main button (start RACE, pause RESUME, results NEXT RACE). A button's Space activation is the keydown/keyup default, which is cancelled. Sequence: createGame(root) -> menu shows, RACE focused -> press Space -> keydown bubbles to window, onDown calls preventDefault, keyup is prevented too (down.delete returns true) -> no click, race doesn't start. On main Space wasn't in KEY_MAP, so it worked. Enter still works, so only Space is dead. Repro in a happy-dom game test (tests/game/pause.test.ts setup): `const e = new KeyboardEvent('keydown',{code:'Space',bubbles:true,cancelable:true}); raceButton.dispatchEvent(e); expect(e.defaultPrevented).toBe(false)` fails (true).
findings.suggestedFix: In onDown, leave Space alone (no preventDefault, no latch) when it isn't already held and the target is an interactive element: `if (k.code === ACTION_KEY) { if (!down.has(k.code) && (k.target as Element | null)?.closest?.('button, a, input, select, textarea')) return; ... }`. Keep onUp as is, since it only prevents keyups whose keydown it handled; a Space held across the results overlay still can't click NEXT RACE. The AC7 tests dispatch on a bare EventTarget, so they still pass. Alternatively pass an `actionEnabled: () => mode === 'race' && !paused` option from game.ts.

findings.claim: A Space tap made while the race is paused stays latched and fires the boost on the first tick after resume. Only the pause branch of setPaused resets the input; the resume branch doesn't, and the Space listener is live while paused.
findings.evidence: game.ts:164-175: `if (paused) { stopLoop(); input.reset(); ui.pause(); } else { ui.resume(); startLoop(); }`. keyboard.ts:52-56 latches `actionTapped = true` on any Space keydown, paused or not. Sequence on Dust Bowl: drive through a box so racers[0].armed is true; Esc (pause, input.reset()); press and release Space on the pause card (e.g. trying to activate the focused RESUME; `down` is cleared on keyup but actionTapped stays true); Esc (resume); the next frame runs game.ts:230 `tick(r, input.read())`, which returns `action: true`, and stepWorld fires: racers[0].boostTicks becomes 90 and armed false on the first tick after resume. Without the Space press while paused, armed stays true. Reproducible with tests/game/pause.test.ts helpers (esc(), runFrames(), game.state().race.racers[0]).
findings.suggestedFix: Call `input.reset()` in the resume branch of setPaused before `startLoop()`, as the pause branch and startRace already do. This also clears latches from the pause.

findings.claim: decodeInputs defines `action` with Object.defineProperty as a non-enumerable property. Decoded frames therefore don't deep-equal the inputs that were encoded, and `action` is lost by spread, Object.keys, JSON.stringify and structuredClone. Any consumer that copies decoded frames silently drops every fired boost, and the replay diverges. This conflicts with AC6 ('encode->decode gives action: true back').
findings.evidence: replay.ts:96-98 `// Non-enumerable ... if ((flags & FLAG_ACTION) !== 0) Object.defineProperty(input, 'action', { value: true, writable: true, configurable: true });`. The comment says it exists so the old test replay.test.ts:63 (bit 2 set decodes to `{steer:0,throttle:true,brake:true}` under toEqual) keeps passing. Repro: `const frames=[[{steer:0,throttle:true,brake:false,action:true}]]; const d=decodeInputs(encodeInputs(frames,1),1,1); expect(d).toEqual(frames)` fails (3 enumerable keys vs 4); `{...d[0][0]}.action` is undefined; JSON.stringify(d) has no "action". Determinism trace: take pickup-replay.test.ts's recorded Dust Bowl run with one fired boost and step a world with `replayInputs(replay).map(f => f.map(i => ({...i})))`; boostTicks never reaches 90, so the final carViews differ from the live run, while runReplay matches.
findings.suggestedFix: Don't hide the flag in the decoded frame. The only way to satisfy both replay.test.ts:63 and AC6 is to keep `decodeInputs(text,ticks,carCount)` ignoring bit 2 by default and add an opt-in parameter that sets an ordinary enumerable `action: true`. Have replayInputs()/runReplay() use that opt-in, and cover it with a new test that spreads and deep-compares the frames.

findings.claim: setPowerUp(true) calls panel.insertBefore(powerUp, pause) unconditionally. race-ui.ts calls it on every sync, so on a pickup track the already-placed SPACE · POWER-UP item is removed and re-inserted every animation frame. This breaks the 'a frame where nothing changed touches no DOM' invariant that race-ui.ts documents and that tests/ui/race-ui.test.ts:63 enforces for non-pickup views.
findings.evidence: race-ui.ts:151 `legend.setPowerUp(view.pickups !== undefined);` runs inside sync(), which game.ts:193 calls from draw() once per frame. keycap-legend.ts:63-66 `setPowerUp(on) { if (on) panel.insertBefore(powerUp, pause); else powerUp.remove(); }` has no `if (on === current) return` guard, unlike the sibling setFirstLap (:58-60) and touch.setAction (`if (next === armed) return`). Per the DOM spec, inserting a node that is already a child first removes it, so each call is a childList removal plus addition (style/layout invalidation, MutationObserver records). Repro: copy race-ui.test.ts:63-72 with a view carrying `pickups:[true]` and `racers[0].armed=false`; sync twice with a MutationObserver on document.body; `takeRecords()` is non-empty where the non-pickup version gives 0. A spy on `Node.prototype.insertBefore` counts one call per sync.
findings.suggestedFix: Track the state and return early: `let powerUpOn = false; setPowerUp(on) { if (on === powerUpOn) return; powerUpOn = on; if (on) panel.insertBefore(powerUp, pause); else powerUp.remove(); }`.

checked.target: src/sim/pickups.ts + world.ts stepWorld (tick order, boost/respawn counts)
checked.how: Traced beginPickupTick -> stepCars -> collectPickups -> tick++. Fire tick sets boostTicks 90 and ticks 0..89 are boosted, so exactly 90 boosted ticks and views read 90..0. A taken box is false for exactly 300 views. Armed player never collects (no stacking). Only car 0 reads action. No Math.random/Date/wall clock in new sim code.

checked.target: src/sim/car.ts BOOSTED tuning and AC4 numbers
checked.how: v=min(topSpeed, v+accel*(1-u^2)*DT) tops out near 31.5 after 90 ticks from 25, never above 32. After the boost the excess decays at 2.2/s: 6.5*exp(-4.4) gives about 25.08 within 120 ticks, under 25.5. grep stepCars: other callers use the default boosted=-1.

checked.target: Tracks without pickups (AC5), replays and bot laps
checked.how: createPickups returns undefined for an empty layout, so world.pickups is absent and raceView adds no keys; stepWorld skips the pickup code and ignores a live `action`. gates.md shows G2 +0.0% and G3 5 replays matching. The builder's Bramble Bends test compares views with action pressed every tick.

checked.target: dust-bowl.json pickups vs geometry; validateTrack/buildTrack pickups
checked.how: Width 11 gives max |lateral| 4.5; pickups use +-3.5. Rows at at=0.04 and 0.47 are before the ramp foot (0.09) and outside its 25-unit run-out, and clear of prop rows. Layout uses (cos h, sin h) = right of forward, same as propRows. Error messages name pickups[i].at / .lateral.

checked.target: src/input/index.ts read(), keyboard/touch latches, game.ts loop
checked.how: read() consumes both latches on every call. game.frame reads once per tick, countdown ticks included, so a tap is consumed there; extra ticks in a frame read false. input.reset() runs on startRace and on pause; touch zones are [] while paused. A Space held across the results overlay is still keyup-prevented by onUp. Problems found: F1, F2.

Walked null->false->true->false->null: slot created/removed, ids and zone cache invalidated, aria-disabled toggled, is-popping set on the armed rising edge and cleared by a timer, timers cleared in destroy. A non-pickup race removes the button on its first sync (4 zones). Slide-to-switch and nearest-zone hit test with action above GAS follow the existing semantics.

Equal specificity (0,2,0) and is-resting comes later, so an armed button that has rested (4 s after the pop) is hollow like the unarmed one. The plan audit says to share resting behaviour with the other controls and the screenshots show the active mustard state, so I treated it as a design decision, not a finding.

checked.target: src/render/scene.ts pickups group, props.ts PICKUP, game.ts draw()
checked.how: One mesh plus hull and one shadow per layout pickup, same order as layout.pickups. Visibility is set from view.pickups on every draw(), including the one in startRace after scene.reset(), so a reused scene shows all boxes on retry. Shadow y and offset match the prop shadows. Shared geometry disposal is safe.

Button and legend state are set from the view on each sync, so nothing stale survives reset or NEXT RACE after the first frame. Armed/unarmed stage screenshots at 844x390 and 1440x900 show the mustard and dirt roundels and the SPACE · POWER-UP key. Fixture positions repeat 3 for two racers, with no visible effect.

checked.target: guardrails/cheats/teleport.patch vs world.ts (owner note, outside R2, not a finding)
checked.how: The patch context line `stepCars(world.cars, clean, world.track);` no longer exists in stepWorld, so harness/scripts/self-test.sh `git apply --cached` will fail for that cheat once this merges. It is a protected file, so the owner would need to refresh it.
